summary:
# NOTES: THE BOROUGH TREASURER (J. S. Fletcher, 1921; Gutenberg #20630). Single book, 31 chapters.

## Setting / cast
- Highmarket, northern English dale town (~5,000 people), main street; Shawl = wooded hill west of town with fir/pine, limestone crags; Hobwick Quarry on moor; High Gill junction (railway); Norcaster = county town/assizes/gaol; Wilchester = southern town where 1881 crime happened; Darlington = Stoner's home; Woking; Hexendale = valley village over moors; Good Folks' Lift = moor rise.
- **Anthony Mallalieu** (real name John Mallows): Mayor of Highmarket (2nd term), big, fleshy, 50-60, small sly eyes, gold chain, silk hat, silver-headed oak stick. Partner.
- **Milford Cotherstone** (real name Mark Chidforth): Borough Treasurer (6th yr), slight, wiry, nervous, thin whitening hair. Daughter **Lettie** (Letitia). Partners own Mallalieu & Cotherstone, Builders & Contractors, yard by gateway on main street; both houses on Shawl slope.
- **Herbert "Bert" Stoner**: clerk, 22-27, salary £2 12s 6d/wk; lodges with Mrs. Battley; friend **David Myler** (Darlington commercial traveller, wife a Wilchester girl); Myler's father-in-law **Mr. Pursey** (apple-faced, Wilchester) and mother-in-law Mrs. Maria Pursey.
- **Windle Bent**: rich manufacturer, Lettie's fiancé, Parliamentary ambitions; school friend **Gifford Brereton** (London barrister, dark, olive complexion, Harborough's defender). Bent's house across from Mallalieu's.
- **Mr. Kitely** (ex-detective, ~35 yrs police service; cottage at top of Shawl; rents from Cotherstone £25/yr, pays quarterly £6 5s); housekeeper **Miss Pett** (tall gaunt, parchment skin, bright black eyes, red-and-yellow turban, toothless; ex-Major Stilman's housekeeper at Kandahar Cottage, Woking; earlier linen-keeper Mervyn Crescent Kensington, storekeeper Royal Belvedere Bayswater; from Oakbarrow Farm near Horsham; in India 10 yrs, charged with strangling Eurasian girl with silk handkerchief, acquitted).
- **Christopher Pett**: nephew, solicitor, 23B Cursitor Street, sly, thin white hands, "Popham & Pilboody" connection.
- **John (Jack) "Gentleman Jack" Harborough**: pig-killer, poacher, mysterious; daughter **Avice Harborough** (grey eyes, governess to Northrop children). Cottage at far end of Shawl, thatched; greased cratch cords on shed verandah.
- **Dr. Rockcliffe**: police surgeon. **Superintendent** (unnamed). **Sergeant**; observant policeman **George**. **Councillor Northrop** (magistrate, shrewd little man). **Tallington**: Highmarket solicitor. **Garthwaite**: neighbour who found Kitely. **Postick**: bill-poster. **Popsie**: barmaid at Grey Mare. **Rellit**: ironmonger. **Stilby/Gradston**: Norcaster solicitor/barrister for Cotherstone. **Carfax**: London solicitor (Duke's Head Hotel, Norcaster); inquiry agents **Stobb** and **Leykin** (ex-Scotland Yard). **Mr. John Wraythwaite of Wraye** (bearded, tall, Australian sheep fortune, foster-brother of Harborough; new Squire). **Mrs. Susan Hamthwaite**: old moor woman, poacher, witness.

## BOOK / Plot in order
1. **Blackmail (Ch I)**: Oct afternoon, Mallalieu & Cotherstone inspect new carts (patent release pin). Kitely pays rent; reveals he recognized them: "In the dock—at Wilchester Assizes." 30 yrs ago, Building Society fraud (Mallalieu treasurer, Cotherstone secretary), £2000, 2 yrs. Demands annuity; "I'll come in here again tomorrow afternoon." Mentions Lettie & Bent's marriage.
2. **Crime and Success (Ch II)**: Cotherstone reflects; they'd hidden money; left for Liverpool; bought Highmarket business. Cotherstone tells Mallalieu at office; Mallalieu: "Gad!" Plan to pay blackmail. Clerk **Stoner** notices Cotherstone's whisky, glass, 6 sovereigns on desk.
3. **Murder (Ch III)**: Cotherstone agonises; wishes Kitely dead. Telephone from Lettie: supper at 8 with Bent and friend Brereton. Supper; Bent says Kitely has been tracing Bent's pedigree (Town Clerk, borough charters). Cotherstone leaves ~8:50 for an hour. Returns ~10. Garthwaite arrives: Kitely strangled in coppice above Cotherstone's house.
4. **The Pine Wood (Ch IV)**: Cotherstone shaken. Cotherstone leads group straight to body (Brereton notices). Body behind limestone rock; pine-needle drag marks; running-knot cord, "a single twist and a turn." Dr. Rockcliffe: killer had knot experience. Brereton suggests Thuggee. Miss Pett at cottage: red-yellow turban, "There's naught can upset or frighten me." Cotherstone: "There's a clue!"
5. **The Cord (Ch V)**: Cord is pig-killer's cord from the cratch. Miss Pett: Kitely took pension at bank that noon, carried money, gold watch & chain (~£100), pocket-book with papers. Warned him about walking. Police go to Harborough's; Avice appears.
6. **The Mayor (Ch VI)**: Avice: father out; "murdered? Shot?" Shed cord freshly cut, coil on nail. Brereton: "Nobody but a fool would..." Meet Mallalieu walking home from Northrop's whist (at 10). Mallalieu's shock. Mallalieu goes to police.
7. **Night Work (Ch VII)**: Mallalieu's reasoning: Cotherstone guilty, frame Harborough. Bank manager: Harborough was at counter when Kitely drew money, changed a £5 note. Doctor: knot expertise. Mallalieu at office next morning with Cotherstone ("So long as nobody but him knew..."). Policeman: "They've brought Harborough down."
8. **Retained for the Defence (Ch VIII)**: Harborough refuses alibi ("I shan't tell"); crescent steel from boot toe found at scene. Avice, Northrop: Brereton offers to defend free. Northrop: Mallalieu & cards; Northrop passed Shawl ~9:45. Brereton: Cotherstone absent one hour.
9. **Antecedents (Ch IX)**: Magistrates' hearing; cash £20+ gold in wash-leather bag found on Harborough. Miss Pett in witness box: 83 Acacia Grove Camberwell; nephew Christopher Pett, 23B Cursitor Street; will left to Miss Pett. Harborough: "Go back, sir—go inch by inch, through Kitely's life!"
10. **The Hole in the Thatch (Ch X)**: Bent & Brereton dine; Brereton plans to stay for Norcaster Assizes. Brereton reasons Cotherstone knew location. Police search finds £15 notes (three £5 notes) and papers hidden in thatch hole of Harborough's shed. Memorandum: "M. & C. v. S. B. cir. 81."
11. **Christopher Pett (Ch XI)**: Brereton's electric torch theory. Pett visits Bent's with will (Kitely's estate to Miss Pett, ~£150 p.a. Brixton house property); codicil legacy to Bent: Kitely's scrap-book. Ironmonger Rellit: torches sold only to Vicar's son, Mallalieu, Harborough.
12. **Parental Anxiety (Ch XII)**: Mallalieu & Cotherstone quarrel in office ("you think I did that job"). Cotherstone visits doctor, feigns heart trouble; asks Bent & Lettie to marry early; Lettie resists, Bent promises. Bent asks Brereton about special licences.
13. **The Anonymous Letter (Ch XIII)**: Harborough committed for trial. Pett harasses Brereton. Registered letter (London postmark, typewritten): £900 (six £150 notes) to fund defence; reward advertisement via *The Times*: "Highmarket Exchequer needs replenishing." Avice: not surprised. Reward £500 posted via solicitor Tallington. Stoner sees bill.
14. **The Sheet of Figures (Ch XIV)**: Stoner (27) finds Cotherstone's scribbled sheet: compound interest of £2000 at 3.5%/5%, word "Wilchester" repeated. Stoner's Darlington friend Myler knows Wilchester. Stoner plans for Darlington.
15. **One Thing Leads to Another (Ch XV)**: Stoner at Myler's; Mr. Pursey recounts Mallows & Chidforth case (1881, building society, £2000, 2 yrs). Myler: take reward, don't blackmail. Stoner resolves to blackmail.
16. **The Lonely Moor (Ch XVI)**: Stoner returns Sunday via High Gill, meets Mallalieu on moor by Hobwick Quarry spinney; blackmail; Stoner names "Mallows and Chidforth"; Mallalieu strikes his temple with oak stick; Stoner falls through rotten railings down quarry. Mallalieu kicks stick over edge, flees; leaves stick.
17. **The Medical Opinion (Ch XVII)**: Mallalieu worries about stick; Stoner absent; body found in Hobwick Quarry. Doctor: skull blow killed him; ticket-collector: Stoner returned Sunday 3:03 train. Brereton copies pocket-book entry: "M. & C.—fraud—bldg. soc.—Wilchester Assizes—81—£2000—money never recovered—2 yrs.—K. pres."
18. **The Scrap Book (Ch XVIII)**: Brereton finds Kitely scrap-book: 1881 report, *Wilchester Sentinel*, "Mallows and Chidforth"; Kitely's 1884 note. Brereton goes to Hamthwaite-bound walk with Avice; invited via note from Susan Hamthwaite.
19. **A Tall Man in Grey Clothes (Ch XIX)**: Brereton tells Avice his theory; Avice reveals Mallalieu harassed her and Harborough a year before. Hamthwaite: saw Harborough at Good Folks' Lift ~8:50–9:50 Kitely night with tall man in grey clothes, grey-bearded, going to Hexendale. Brereton: tall man sent the £900. Bent tells: wedding set for next week.
20. **At Bay (Ch XX)**: Brereton goes to Tallington; Bent told; Cotherstone called in. Cotherstone confesses (Chidforth), blames Mallows; paid £2000 + 4% interest (£4400) back day after Kitely murder; says Mallalieu killed Stoner (he saw from bush). Superintendent arrests both.
21. **The Interrupted Flight (Ch XXI)**: Mallalieu searches for stick at quarry; plans to flee via Town Council water-supply trip to sister town; keeps securities in special waistcoat. Arrested at Town Hall committee.
22. **The Hand in the Darkness (Ch XXII)**: Mallalieu's hearing: Myler and Pursey testify; sweethearts testify; bail refused. Mallalieu escapes via Town Hall private stair, into orchard, woods; Miss Pett grabs his wrist: "Miss Pett."
23. **Comfortable Captivity (Ch XXIII)**: Miss Pett hides him in Kitely's room (pictures of judges, "Dying Speech and Confession" broadsheet). Toddy drugged; she takes waistcoat, counts money (~£ in securities/bank-notes/gold).
24. **Strict Business Lines (Ch XXIV)**: Christopher Pett arrives; sold Kitely's Brixton property £3,417 5s 11d; costs £61 2s 9d; commission £100 (Miss Pett's). Plan: Mallalieu to escape to Norcaster in furniture van. Mallalieu offers £50 each.
25. **No Further Evidence (Ch XXV)**: Cotherstone in Norcaster gaol, aims to clear himself; Lettie calm, wedding postponed. Inquest on Stoner: Cotherstone testifies against Mallalieu; verdict wilful murder against Mallalieu. Cotherstone discharged (prosecution withdraws).
26. **The Virtues of Suspicion (Ch XXVI)**: Christopher lies to Mallalieu; Mallalieu suspects drugging; pours toddy into flower-pot; sleeps with revolver.
27. **Mr. Wraythwaite of Wraye (Ch XXVII)**: Brereton summoned to Duke's Head Hotel, Norcaster, by Carfax; takes Avice. Wraythwaite of Wraye: Harborough's alibi; heir to Wraye (father secretly married Harborough's aunt; Harborough & Wraythwaite foster-brothers).
28. **Pages from the Past (Ch XXVIII)**: Stobb reports Miss Pett: Major Stilman died in bed with drugs (inquest, misadventure); left £2000 and furniture to Miss Pett. Leykin: India strangling of Eurasian girl with silk handkerchief. Carfax will take inquiry agents to Highmarket police.
29. **Without Thought of Consequence (Ch XXIX)**: Mallalieu, awake, realizes waistcoat searched; shoots Miss Pett (as she approaches waistcoat) and Christopher Pett in passage; fires twice; then dresses; hears knocking; sees Cotherstone among men outside.
30. **Cotherstone (Ch XXX)**: Cotherstone on Town Hall steps, shouted taunts ("King's evidence!"). Drinks champagne at Highmarket Arms with barrister (the "Felons' Friend"). Club alderman turns him away. Cotherstone visits superintendent: confesses Miss Pett's threat (saw Christopher present on the night of Kitely's murder, Miss Pett said "You and your partner are much more likely to have killed Kitely"). Superintendent and Cotherstone go to cottage. Shots fired; Mallalieu opens door, shoots Cotherstone dead, then himself.
31. **The Barrister's Fee (Ch XXXI)**: Six months later (May). Bents married, went abroad. Brereton visits Avice at Wraye steward's house (Harborough steward/agent). Proposal to leave Wraye; "we shall come back to it now and then—together!" THE END.

## Key facts / quotes
- "Highmarket Exchequer needs replenishing" (Times ad). Reward £500, doubled if needed.
- Cord: "pig-killer's cord," cratch.
- Cotherstone's prime quote: "Because I saw Mallalieu fell Stoner!"
- Miss Pett's surname spelling in court: "83, Acacia Grove, Camberwell."
- Stoner killed Sunday; ticket-collector saw him 3:03 train; quarry ~4:30.
